answer: Proof-of-Stake protocols mitigate Sybil attacks by requiring agents to lock capital as collateral, turning identity creation into a cost-prohibitive financial endeavor. An attacker cannot simply whisper new addresses into existence to sway an island of nodes; they must acquire significant stake to gain influence. This economic barrier functions like a mechanical raven, tirelessly stripping voting weight from malicious actors who cannot sustain the ongoing fiscal burden of securing a network consensus.
